title: Prove pre-commit crash recovery by re-upload

gates.name: Python typecheck
gates.command: docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend python -m mypy src/face_moment

gates.name: Crash recovery tests
gates.command: docker compose run --rm backend python -m pytest tests/inventory/test_crash_recovery.py

evidence_required: FT-001-AC-005 RED: after dependency completion, an isolated pre-commit termination yields at least one claim-equivalent failure: a Photo or pending row survives, media becomes browser-accessible, or ordinary re-upload cannot complete exactly one normal admission; PRE_IMPLEMENTATION_GREEN: if the first safe probe already leaves zero database rows, keeps any orphan private and permits one complete re-upload, preserve that result and make no unnecessary production-behavior change; GREEN: the same probe satisfies all three observations; decisive comparison: post-crash database count is zero, forbidden access is absent and post-re-upload count is one complete pair; artifact: isolated fault-injection timeline, database projection and object-access probe.
purpose: Establish the accepted KISS recovery behavior for the object-upload/PostgreSQL pre-commit crash window as its own sibling outcome.
success_outcome: A pre-commit process failure leaves no database admission or exposed media, and ordinary photographer re-upload succeeds without an orphan lifecycle or distributed transaction.
anti_goals: Do not implement orphan scanning/cleanup, durable upload resume, outbox, object move/copy or distributed transaction emulation.
Do not adopt duplicate or atomic-publication claims beyond trusting their completed outcomes.

forbidden_scope: Orphan cleanup lifecycle or background job
Production process termination or non-disposable storage
stop_conditions: The crash probe cannot be isolated, safely rerun or limited to task-owned disposable state.
A successful verdict would require cleanup/recovery machinery excluded by the accepted contract.
The failure injection could affect operator/default or production resources.

constraints: The probe starts from known disposable PostgreSQL/MinIO state, records the injection point and cleans only task-owned recoverable data.
A possible orphan remains private and is not required to be deleted for success.
Recovery is one ordinary re-upload through the existing admission boundary.
invariants: Pre-commit failure creates no Photo or pending row.
No orphan object is browser-accessible or authoritative without committed PostgreSQL state.
Re-upload yields one normal complete admission without a recovery subsystem.
verification_targets: A safe isolated fault-injection probe records known initial state, crash point, zero database admission, private orphan observation, successful re-upload and owned cleanup.
